# Area: Client Runtime

## Surface

Who consumes this: `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client` callers (`createHevyClient` Promise API used by Node, CLI, Worker, and tests); `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client/internal` Effect request facade used by `@hevy-mcp/operations`; Worker bearer/OAuth validation via `validateHevyApiKeyResilient` in `packages/worker/src/validation-cache.ts`. End users never call this package directly; MCP tools and the CLI collapse through these Promise/Effect boundaries.

How it is tested: vitest in `packages/hevy-client` and `packages/worker`; TestClock and fake timers for delays; mocked `fetch` (no live Hevy in this area).

Focused suites:
- `packages/hevy-client/src/hevy-client.test.ts`
- `packages/hevy-client/src/internal-request-effect.test.ts`
- `packages/hevy-client/src/request-effect.test.ts`
- `packages/hevy-client/src/request-local-retry-state.test.ts`
- `packages/hevy-client/src/retry-schedule.test.ts`
- `packages/hevy-client/src/backoff.test.ts`
- `packages/hevy-client/src/endpoint-policy.test.ts`
- `packages/worker/src/validation-cache.test.ts`

## Interactions enumerated

- Construct `createHevyClient({ apiKey, baseUrl?, fetch?, timeoutMs?, maxGetRetries?, sleep?, onLog?, onRequestStart?, onRequestComplete?, onRetryWait? })`.
- Call any of the 22 Promise methods with optional `{ signal, deadline, timeoutMs }`.
- Receive a successful JSON body, or a rejected `HevyHttpError` with `code` / `status` / execution metadata.
- Observe retries: transient GET/HEAD/OPTIONS reads and PUT/DELETE idempotent writes retry; POST/PATCH non-idempotent writes never retry.
- Observe retry budget: default `maxGetRetries = 3` (4 attempts); delays start at 300 ms, double each retry, cap at 5000 ms, plus bounded jitter.
- Observe 429 handling: client retries 429 and honors `Retry-After` as a lower bound, still jittered, clipped to remaining deadline.
- Observe per-attempt timeout and overall operation deadline.
- Observe the one extra read attempt after a client-derived attempt deadline. Caller-supplied `deadline` is never extended.
- Abort via `AbortSignal`: already-aborted, mid-fetch, while reading the body, during backoff. Concurrent requests stay isolated.
- Consume the internal Effect facade: same retry/timeout/abort counts; tagged errors.
- Operations pass `descriptor.safety` into composed Hevy calls; raw client calls fall back to HTTP-method mapping.
- Worker `validateHevyApiKeyResilient`: cache hit skips Hevy; miss validates; retries transient failures with delays `[300, 600]`; never retries 429; abort/deadline stop the loop; cache never stores the raw API key.

## Assertions

### VAL-CLIENT-001: Happy-path GET returns parsed JSON and sends api-key
A `getWorkouts` / `getUserInfo` / equivalent GET against a 200 JSON response resolves to the parsed body. The outbound request uses the configured `baseUrl` (default `https://api.hevyapp.com`), path under `/v1/`, query params, and an `api-key` header equal to the constructor `apiKey`. Exactly one `fetch` call occurs when the first response is 2xx.
Tool: vitest
Evidence: test names `uses object-form options and safely encodes requests`, `forwards every curated operation through its generated API wrapper`; terminal output of `packages/hevy-client/src/hevy-client.test.ts`; no `HEVY_API_KEY` in logs.

### VAL-CLIENT-002: All 22 public Promise methods remain callable
Each method on `HevyClient` returns a `Promise` and, given a 200, resolves without throwing. `createRoutine` may resolve `undefined` when the body is empty. The public object has no enumerable `requestEffect`. Existing Promise signatures (`signal`, `deadline`, `timeoutMs`) keep working.
Tool: vitest
Evidence: test names `forwards every curated operation through its generated API wrapper`, `keeps the public HevyClient Promise-only at type and runtime`; 22 `fetch` calls in the wrapper test.

### VAL-CLIENT-003: Default timeout is 60 seconds
With no constructor `timeoutMs` and no per-call `timeoutMs`/`deadline`, a hanging fetch is not aborted before 60_000 ms of attempt budget. The observable default attempt timeout remains one minute.
Tool: vitest
Evidence: test name `allows slow collection endpoints a one-minute default deadline`.

### VAL-CLIENT-004: Per-call timeoutMs overrides the client default
A client constructed with a short `timeoutMs` still succeeds when the method is called with a larger `{ timeoutMs }` that covers the mocked latency.
Tool: vitest
Evidence: test name `allows a per-operation timeout override`.

### VAL-CLIENT-005: Hanging fetch times out as HEVY_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED
When `fetch` never settles and no caller `deadline` is set, the Promise rejects with `HevyHttpError` `{ code: "HEVY_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED", outcome: "deadline_exceeded", phase: "dispatch" }`.
Tool: vitest
Evidence: test name `times out when fetch never settles`.

### VAL-CLIENT-006: Hanging response body times out as HEVY_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED
When headers return 200 but the body stream never completes, the Promise rejects with `{ code: "HEVY_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED", outcome: "deadline_exceeded", phase: "response-content" }`.
Tool: vitest
Evidence: test name `times out while consuming a response body`.

### VAL-CLIENT-007: One free read retry after a client-derived attempt deadline
On a read (GET) with `maxGetRetries > 0` and no caller `deadline`, the first attempt-timeout is followed by exactly one more fetch with a fresh attempt budget. That extra attempt does not emit `onLog` message `"Retrying Hevy API request"` and does not open `onRetryWait`. If the second attempt returns 200, the method resolves. Observation sequence includes `deadline_exceeded` then `success`. This remains true if the implementation folds the extra attempt into schedule composition: consumers still see one extra read fetch, no backoff sleep, no retry log.
Tool: vitest
Evidence: test name `retries a read once with a fresh deadline budget after a deadline`.

### VAL-CLIENT-008: Free read retry is bounded and not repeated
If the extra read attempt also times out, the rejection is `{ code: "HEVY_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED", outcome: "deadline_exceeded" }` and `fetch` is called exactly twice. After that extra attempt, a subsequent HTTP 500 is reported as `status: 500` / `outcome: "terminal_failure"`, not as another deadline, and is not retried again.
Tool: vitest
Evidence: test names `returns the deadline error when the bounded read retry also times out`, `does not misclassify a non-deadline retry failure as deadline exceeded`, `uses one timeout budget for hanging response bodies`.

### VAL-CLIENT-009: Caller-supplied deadline is never extended
`getWorkout(..., { deadline })` against a hanging fetch fails with `HEVY_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED` after a single fetch. No retry log, no sleep, no retry-wait. An already-elapsed `{ deadline: Date.now() - 1 }` or `{ deadline: 0 }` rejects with `{ code: "HEVY_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED", phase: "before-dispatch" }` and does not call `fetch`.
